items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/audit.rs's `run_check` (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.

items.title: Default starter rule set: docs and code-quality style adopters begin with
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

items.title: Capture-file citations for oversized report evidence
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 1: task-4-report.json reached 583KB because all 41 tdd entries embed verbatim RED/GREEN inline; reviewers re-ran cycles anyway, and T5's fix round already invented the better shape (bulk evidence in named workspace files, byte-prefix-matching inline excerpts).

Change: let a tdd or live_run entry cite a workspace capture file by path for output beyond a stated size, keeping the first lines plus exit inline; standardize the t5-evidence/ convention in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json and both agent templates. Deferred from batch 16 because template changes trigger process.evals-rerun and the batch was already closing.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Ships in template/tools until the Tier-2 port owns audit (phase 2), then carries into the Rust audit.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.

items.title: release-please misses commits that change the embedded template/ payload but not crates/houserules/**
body: HR-073's release-type: rust at crates/houserules moved release-please's commit attribution off the repository root: CommitSplit.split (commit-split.ts:99) now counts a commit toward the crate's next version only when it touches crates/houserules/**, since the ROOT_PROJECT_PATH special case that used to assign every commit (manifest.ts:700-701) no longer applies. crates/houserules/src/install.rs:232-234 embeds `../../template/` into the shipped binary via #[derive(RustEmbed)], so a commit that changes only template/ (or README.md, or another root-level path) changes shipped code and, under the new attribution, opens no release PR at all.

Measured over v0.2.0-alpha..6aa19e0 (batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review): 82 of 119 commits touch no path under crates/houserules/, and 7 of 27 feat/fix commits are unattributed under the new package path -- four of them (7460c77b feat(template), 6ac1aaa7 fix(template), 719d3f58 fix(tools), 101555ef fix(template)) change the embedded payload directly, per t5-evidence/hr081-template-payload-commits.sh's own enumeration by touched path rather than commit subject (fix round 2: a subject-scoped read of the same range missed 719d3f58, 'fix(tools): validate rejects incomplete terminal reports', which touches no crates/houserules/ path and two template/ files). Today enough crate-side commits ride along that a release PR still opens; a cycle whose only changes are template/, README.md, or the knowledge base would silently ship nothing.

The package path is not the thing to change: release-type rust at '.' (the root) would take the Rust strategy's workspace branch and push a CargoToml update for the root manifest, which cargo-toml.ts:37-40 throws on ('is not a package manifest') since the root Cargo.toml carries no [package] section under this workspace's virtual-manifest shape -- reviewer-confirmed and re-verified by the implementer. The gap needs a different remedy, not a reversal of HR-073's ruling.

Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) an extra-files or component-mapping addition to release-please-config.json that attributes template/** changes to the crate's own path for commit-attribution purposes; (b) a documented pre-release rule that a payload-changing commit always rides alongside a crate-side commit before a release is cut, checked by hand or by a gate. Owner picks.

MECHANISM (task-1 fix round 4, provisional pending owner ratification at the batch report): remedy (b), concretized. crates/houserules/payload.stamp records a sha256 digest of template/'s tracked file set, recomputed and compared by payload-stamp-gate (crates/houserules/src/bin/payload-stamp-gate.rs), wired into mise run lint (houserules.payload-stamp-gate). That gate is a TREE-LEVEL check only: a branch splitting the template/ edit from the stamp regeneration across two commits still passes it at the tip. Fix round 5 closed that gap: houserules check-commit now also runs this entry's own co-change check (if template/**, then crates/houserules/payload.stamp) per commit, over the PR's full range in CI, so a split commit pair fails before merge, not only a stale tree.

Still gating this item's own close: the mechanism above is proven by source-level review and a full-pipeline simulation against real git history (batch-24 task-1's own t1-evidence/), never by a genuine release-please run. The first real template-only change that lands on main after T2 -- one commit touching template/ and crates/houserules/payload.stamp together, nothing else -- is that live proof.
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), important finding 1.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 1 review (minor issue 8): check-backlog's round-trip finding (HR-076) names a concrete remedy per file class, but only backlog/items/*.json has a shipped command that can reach it (`houserules set`). The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.

items.title: Main needs the code owner's approval for everyone but the owner; Dependabot auto-merge runs on the owner's token
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: only the owner merges to main without an approval; every other contributor's PR needs the owner's approving review. Applied as a second ruleset `approval` on the default branch (one approving review, code-owner review required, stale reviews dismissed on push, threads resolved) whose only bypass actor is the repository admin role. The first ruleset `main` (the eight required checks incl. CodeQL, linear history, no force-push, PR required) keeps no bypass and binds the owner too. GitHub cannot exempt one rule inside a ruleset, hence the split.

Consequence and the ruled fix: GitHub refuses the Actions app as a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, so a merge enabled with GITHUB_TOKEN now waits for an approval and the HR-092 auto-merge stalls. The owner chose the token route: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables auto-merge with a fine-grained personal access token of the owner (Contents and Pull requests read/write on this repository only), stored as the Dependabot secret DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (a Dependabot-triggered workflow reads that store, not Actions secrets). A merge performed as the owner also starts the push workflows on main, which lifts HR-092's GITHUB_TOKEN limit for these merges.

PENDING proof: the next minor or patch Dependabot PR merging on its own with the workflow green. Flip to done with that PR's number. HR-068 (a token for the release flow) stays a separate ruling: release-please edits a workflow file, which needs the `workflows` permission this token does not carry.

items.title: `get` only resolves HR-/A-/PP- ids; a project's own --id-prefix is not respected
body: `is_backlog_id` (crates/houserules/src/get.rs) hardcodes the HR-/A-/PP- id shapes rather than reading the project's own stamped id prefix (`.houserules.json`'s `idPrefix`, default `WI`). Reproduced live at batch 22 T1: `houserules init --dir <scratch>` with no `--id-prefix` seeds `WI-nnn` items, and `houserules get WI-001` then fails with `unknown id "WI-001"` even though the item exists and `list`/`batch` both resolve it fine.
Found incidentally while live-running HR-105's archive sweep (docs/plans/2026-09-11-batch-22-stewardship.md, T1); out of that task's own scope, so filed here rather than fixed in place.

Consequence recorded at batch 22 T1 fix round 1 (task-1-review.json, issue 3): this gap is not only latent. houserules archive makes it active -- a WI-prefixed item's archived record becomes unreachable by get in ANY project once swept, not merely unreached before the sweep the way it was before HR-105. get's own archive fallback works around the consequence by trying both archive lookups regardless of routing (fix round 1); this item still tracks the underlying matcher fix.

items.title: find-shell-tool-refs.rs carries two exception entries that now match nothing
body: `exceptions()` in crates/houserules/src/bin/find-shell-tool-refs.rs names two exceptions -- `template/tools/kb.mjs` and `crates/houserules/src/rules/read.rs` -- that a live run (`cargo run --bin find-shell-tool-refs`) shows currently matching zero hits: kb.mjs no longer exists in the tree, and read.rs's own sole `kb.sh`-naming line was removed by the batch 22 T3a comment sweep. Only the `install.rs` exception still fires (4 hits).

Found while sweeping this file's comments at batch 22 T3b: correcting a stale doc claim about read.rs's hit count surfaced that the underlying exception entry is now dead weight, not only the sentence describing it.

Removing the two dead `Exception` entries (and `RUST_FILES`'s `rules/read.rs` member, if nothing else in that file still needs the scan) is a code change, out of scope for a comment-only sweep; filed here rather than fixed in place.

The surviving `install.rs` exception's own `reason` string literal narrates its own history (batch/phase/fix-round references) the same way the two removed entries' reasons did. It is user-facing output, not a comment, so the comment-only sweep correctly left it alone -- but once the two dead entries are deleted, rewrite this one's `reason` to the present-tense rule it states (RETIRED's own doc/test are FILE PATHS the deletion mechanism removes, narrowed to exactly that window so a whole-file exception cannot swallow an unrelated hit) in the same commit.

items.title: .gitattributes carries the same history narration HR-106's keep/drop line prunes from code
body: HR-106's keep/drop line (docs/specs/2026-09-11-batch-22-stewardship.md §3) drops batch/task/round references, commit SHAs, and CI run/job ids from comments, keeping only the current constraint. The repository root's own .gitattributes carries exactly that class of history narration in its four comment blocks, confirmed present at HEAD: PR #6 and CI run 34056471594 (the tests/goldens/** block), commit e36c4b2 (the tests/fixtures/** block, alongside batch 20 T3 and HR-084), commits 0bb27a0 and 2174a9f (the .claude/rules/**/.claude/skills/project-knowledge/** block, alongside batch 20 T6), and HR-054 (the tests/corpus/** block).

Found during HR-106's own T3c comment sweep of crates/houserules/tests/**; .gitattributes is not a code file under any of spec §3's three file lists (crates/houserules/src/**, crates/houserules/tests/**, tools/*.sh, .githooks/*, and the template shell copies), so the sweep left it untouched, per scope.

Prune each block to the current constraint it states (which paths get -text, and why -text specifically, not the discovery history), the same rewrite HR-106's own sweeps already applied across crates/houserules/src/** and crates/houserules/tests/**.

items.title: update restamps an entry whose content equals the current payload
body: Found at the batch-22 close-out update run: an entry edited to the exact content the current payload ships (both copies edited together, the dogfood norm) classifies Modified against its stale baseline and prints 'kept (locally modified)' on every update forever, because only at-baseline entries restamp.

Refinement: when current content equals the current payload content, restamp silently - the adopter holds exactly what the kit ships, so there is nothing to keep or report. Applies to KIT_OWNED files and knowledge entries alike.
Seven such lines print on this repository's own update today; the report noise grows with every ruled wording change.

items.title: Deterministic citation-line check in check-report-claims
body: RULED 2026-09-12 (batch 22 report, standing proposal 1): extend the report-claims gate deterministically - every path:NNN (and path:NNN-MMM) citation in a report's narrative fields must name an existing file, and NNN must not exceed that file's line count at HEAD. Catches the stream-index-as-file-line class (batch 22 T3c: 13 of 33 catalogue citations) and dangling pins mechanically, where judged review rounds catch them today.
Design note: command fields stay exempt (the ephemeral-path precedent); the check reads the tracked tree and the batch workspace the report cites.

items.title: The schema engine silently ignores unsupported keywords - a gate that narrows itself
body: Found at batch 23 T1 review round 2, proven empirically: rules/check.rs's validate handles only $ref, enum, type, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, items, uniqueItems, required, properties, and additionalProperties; any other keyword (oneOf, anyOf, allOf, const, maximum, format) falls through every branch and the field goes UNCHECKED with no finding printed. A scratch schema whose taskNumber carried oneOf stopped raising the 'must be integer or string' error entirely.

This is the class quality.gates-derive-their-scope exists for: a validation gate that narrows itself in silence. It is also what made a review-suggested oneOf fix unimplementable at T1 (the two-descriptions fallback shipped instead).

Remedy, pick one at spec time: the engine reports an unsupported keyword as a named finding (the way an uncompilable pattern already is - houserules.crash-paths-are-named's shape), or it grows real combinator support. The named-finding route is the smaller, safer first step and unblocks combinators later.

items.title: Cross-check numeric and locative claims against their cited captures
body: From the batch-23 branch review retrospective: a sentence in a commit body, report narrative, or plan stating 'N passed', 'N files', or 'the X live in Y' while citing a retained capture should fail a deterministic check when the number or location is absent from that capture. All three batch-23 state-only-the-source instances (523-vs-528, a sweep example failing its own pattern, a plan's marker-location sentence) were one such cross-check away.

items.title: Vacuous-zero check: a cited sweep must cover the file it certifies
body: From the batch-23 branch review retrospective: when a report cites a sweep or enumeration as proof over a file, the audit's report check should verify the sweep's retained file list contains that file and flag the citation otherwise. Batch 23 T1 round 0 cited a sweep whose list omitted deliverable.rs - the file the task changed most - so its zero was vacuous.

items.title: Promote the no-provenance comment sweep into a deterministic gate
body: From the batch-23 branch review retrospective: promote the retained no-provenance sweeps (batch-22 t3a set plus batch-23's per-file variant) into a residue-gate-style deterministic check over crates/**, so provenance narration in comments fails a gate instead of costing an opus review round. The marker classes derive from the retained probes; writing-style.code-comments' history clause is the governing rule.

items.title: The v1-readiness batch: v1 gaps plus the owner's full template-defaults review
body: Owner direction (2026-09-12, during batch 24): the batch AFTER batch 24 (batch 25) makes the repository v1-ready. Two halves.

(1) V1 readiness: the controller proposes everything deemed necessary at shaping. Known candidates to complete then: the macOS-signing revisit-at-1.0 ruling; the CLI/schema surface freeze; the open quality-gate items as v1 gates (HR-107 citation-lines, HR-109 silent-keyword engine, HR-110/111 claim cross-checks, HR-112 no-provenance gate); the matcher and restamp refinements (HR-100, HR-104); docs completeness incl. HR-088/089-class update-path gaps; the 1.0 version cut itself.

(2) The template-defaults review: a complete sweep over every default the template ships. The controller delivers a complete list/spreadsheet - one row per shipped default - where the owner can, per item: tick template-appropriate or not; request changes and specify which; and ADD items they think are still missing. Every owner decision then homes per process.rulings-to-file and the edits ride the batch.

The list's row set derives from template/** itself (git ls-files template/), never from memory: the seeded knowledge entries per topic (process, quality, security-hygiene, writing-style, knowledge-base - every rule, gotcha, and procedure), the three agent templates' instructions, the skills, the schema constraints (id shapes, required fields, textList floors, the task-id shape), the seeded workflow (knowledge.yml), CLAUDE.md's seeded text, settings.json's hooks, areas.json's defaults, backlog seed files, docs/README.md, and the eval scenarios.

Addition (owner, 2026-09-12, same day): the sweep list also carries the GAP rows - items currently in use that are NOT in the template. Two gap sources, each its own row set: (a) this repository's own knowledge/backlog machinery versus template/ (entries, rules, and defaults that exist here but never shipped); (b) the tag-pilot checkout's current state versus template/ - tag-pilot has evolved independently and may hold items that became relevant there without surfacing in houserules. Tag-pilot stays STRICTLY read-only (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only): the sweep READS it to enumerate, never modifies, commits, or runs anything against it. Each gap row gets the same three affordances: adopt into the template or not, with which changes, plus free additions.

Deliverable form settled at shaping: an interactive review page or a spreadsheet file, whichever the owner prefers at the gate; the requirements are the three per-row affordances above plus free additions.

items.title: Vacuous-exception check: a gate exception must match something real
body: Found by batch 24 T3a fix round 1: docs/runbook.md's heading rename from "release-please's release-type" to "release-please configuration" orphaned residue-gate.rs's own named exception -- `runbook_release_please_section_lines` keyed its heading lookup on the old string, so the exception ("docs/runbook.md: the release-please release-type section (HR-073)") could no longer match any real line, while its doc comment kept describing a live, heading-bounded exemption and its two dedicated unit tests (synthetic fixture text carrying the old heading) stayed green throughout, hiding the deadness. The fix round retired the exception, the helper, and both tests outright rather than re-keying: a live `cargo run --bin residue-gate` plus a whole-file grep confirmed docs/runbook.md now carries zero PATTERNS hits anywhere (the retired-Node sweep the same task performed left nothing for any heading-keyed exception to except), so re-keying to the new heading would only have recreated a vacuous exception under a different name.

The systemic gap this leaves: residue-gate.rs's own `exceptions()` mechanism has no way to notice when a declared exception's `matches` predicate excepts zero real hits across a live run -- only a human re-reading the exception list catches it, and this instance survived one heading rename undetected. Same family as HR-111 (a cited sweep must cover the file it certifies): here, a declared exception must cover something the live walk actually finds.

Candidate: after building the excepted/unexpected classification, count each exception's own real (non-test) match total across the live run and warn or fail when any named exception matches zero hits -- the residue-gate binary already computes per-exception hit counts for its own report output ("N hit(s)" per label), so the count exists; only the zero-check does not. Shape (warn vs fail, and whether a zero count for a whole-file exception with no current violations is a false positive the check must tolerate) is open.
Source: batch 24 T3a fix round 1, spec-compliance finding 2 (2026-09-13).

items.title: Template-cluster riders from the batch-24 branch review
body: Three defects for the next template-touching batch (each triggers or adjoins the evals rerun): (1) orchestrating skill - while a task is open, the controller commits only to files disjoint from the task's, records each such commit in the ledger BEFORE the next reviewer dispatch, and the dispatch names them; (2) implementer template / retrieval protocol step 3 - a second, range-wide invocation (check-commit --from $(git merge-base main HEAD) --to HEAD) whenever the diff or id list touches a commits/co-change check, mirroring CI; (3) deliverables schema - an optional rulings array pairing each in-task ruling with its home-file path so homing becomes deterministically checkable.

items.title: Deterministic CI-mirror test for the task-gates list
body: From the batch-24 branch review: a rust test parses .github/workflows/ci.yml's run lines and asserts each named check appears in houserules.task-gates-mirror-ci's own gate list, so the list can no longer silently omit a CI job. Origin: the check-commit job went unnamed and a per-commit check shipped unrun at CI's real --from.

items.title: Wire dist generate --check into a real CI gate for the create-release pairing
body: Batch 24 T3b fix round 1 (task-3b-review.json, important issue 2): crates/houserules/tests/dist_workspace_config.rs pins dist-workspace.toml's create-release = false and release.yml's upload-not-create shape by two independent substrings, with no gate that re-derives one from the other. The file's own doc comment used to claim `dist generate --check` runs in CI and catches drift; it does not. No job in .github/workflows/ci.yml and no task in mise.toml installs or runs `dist` at all, and re-derived live: a scratch clone of the tree at batch 24 T3b fix round 1 with a one-line hand-edit appended to release.yml exits 0 from `dist generate --check` under this repository's own allow-dirty = ["ci"], and exits 255 with an 'out of date contents' diff only once allow-dirty is cleared to []. The comment is corrected to state this plainly; this item tracks making it a real gate instead.

Feasibility, re-derived live at the same fix round: mise's own registry carries cargo-dist (`mise registry | grep dist` -> `aqua:axodotdev/cargo-dist github:axodotdev/cargo-dist cargo:cargo-dist`); `mise install` against a one-line scratch mise.toml (`[tools]\n"cargo-dist" = "0.32.0"`) installed a working `dist` binary via the aqua backend in one step on this Linux development environment, GitHub artifact attestation verified. Linux install is proven; macOS and Windows are not (no such host here), and ci.yml's `rust` job runs a 3-OS matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows) that would also pick up any tool this repository's global mise.toml [tools] table names -- adding cargo-dist there unscoped risks an untested install path on two OSes no existing tool in that table exercises.

Proposed fix: add cargo-dist to mise.toml's [tools], pinned to the same version as dist-workspace.toml's cargo-dist-version (security-hygiene.exact-pins), scoped to the one OS the check actually needs -- mise's own docs name an `os` tool-option for exactly this (mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html, checked 2026-09-13); verify its literal TOML syntax against current docs before use, since the fetched page named the option without a worked example. Add `dist generate --check` as a step in mise.toml's `lint` task (which runs only in ci.yml's ubuntu-only `checks` job, so the rust job's macOS/Windows legs need no new tool at all). Re-run the two exit-code probes above against the real gate (0 clean, 255 on a hand-edit) before shipping, and update dist_workspace_config.rs's doc comment once the gate is real.

Deferred out of batch 24 T3b's fix round per that review's own escape hatch (a full regen gate is shipped only when proven safe wherever it runs; otherwise the honest-comment version plus this deferral note): the CI-wide, 3-OS blast radius of a mise.toml [tools] change is not something to land untested in a fix round with no CI run available here to verify it against first.

items.title: Deterministic audit check: in-branch SHA cited from a permanent file
body: From the batch-24 close branch review (knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs, two occurrences in the batch): flag any 7-40 hex string in a backlog/ or knowledge/ diff hunk that resolves to a commit not reachable from the default branch. Both violations were in-branch SHAs cited from durable files, mechanically detectable at audit time. Companion to HR-117's derive-the-enumeration class (the reviewer also proposed deriving houserules.task-gates-mirror-ci's gate list from ci.yml at audit time; HR-117 already books that class as a rust test).
